propositions: Closing a ticket with verify.require_completion_verification_for_close=true reads HEAD independently during verify and sign phases, allowing a concurrent commit to land between them and split the operations.
When HEAD drifts between verify and sign, the signer correctly refuses to attest the stale tree, but the close transition proceeds anyway, leaving the ticket closed without a completion signature.
The suggested recovery message (re-close to certify) is a no-op for an already-closed ticket, and the only actual recovery paths are --force-close or manual manifest fabrication, both unacceptable.
The default path (no --ref) still reads HEAD twice and remains vulnerable to TOCTOU; the --ref flag only fixed the non-default code path.

A fix must either pin one revision for the entire verify+sign+close unit so unrelated HEAD movement does not invalidate a verified attestation, or abort the close and leave the ticket in_progress when drift is detected.
